statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-85747 (GHSA-685w-q87j-wqw3) is a missing digest check in the github.com/docker/distribution registry client: manifests and blobs fetched by digest were returned without being hashed, so a malicious registry could substitute content. docker/distribution v2.8.3 has no fixed release; the fix shipped in distribution v3.1.2 as commits https://github.com/distribution/distribution/commit/8f91c26c8888a95a36c2357a6e30bc15d4dd76d3 (manifests) and https://github.com/distribution/distribution/commit/93c6e1a3b3c874a73fbd6b8fa9b37577223cff9e (blobs). The docker 29.9.2-r1 packages apply both changes to the registry client vendored in Moby 29.9.2, so dockerd rejects manifest and blob content that does not match the requested digest. The module version reported by go version -m stays v2.8.3+incompatible because the fix is applied to vendored source. Advisory: https://github.com/distribution/distribution/security/advisories/GHSA-685w-q87j-wqw3

The docker 29.9.2-r1 packages apply both changes to the registry client vendored in Moby 29.9.2, so dockerd rejects manifest and blob content that does not match the requested digest. The module version reported by go version -m stays v2.8.3+incompatible because the fix is applied to vendored source. Advisory: https://github.com/distribution/distribution/security/advisories/GHSA-685w-q87j-wqw3

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree (and subpackages), which is frozen upstream with no fixed module release. Scout matches golang.org/x/crypto at the module level because the advisory records the module with no fixed version. The golang-msft-fips toolchain is built from microsoft/go; repository code search shows no import of golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp under src/cmd or elsewhere in src. go.mod lists golang.org/x/crypto as a bootstrap module dependency, but the openpgp subpackage is not compiled into the shipped go/compiler binaries (vulnerable_code_not_present).

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.8 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Alpine 3.23 ships coreutils 9.8, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream unexpand allocation fix from commit b60a159fdc5bfcf9988d3a4cb6f53abe8ad5d35d.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.
